newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end higher, March T-bonds off peaks.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end higher, March T-bonds off peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher, but March T-bonds ended below session peaks due to concerns the U.S. administration would back off from its strong U.S. dollar policy at Saturday's G7 meeting, traders said.

Concerns arose after U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin stated that he believed in a strong U.S. dollar, but that the dollar has been strong "for some time." He also said foreign exchange issues would be a "principal topic" of discussion at the meeting in Berlin.
"The whole key here is that people got spooked by Rubin's comments," one trader said about the slight retreat in bonds.
"What if the G7 came out with some policy against the dollar and everyone is still holding dollars?" he said.
Traders said the higher U.S. dollar was fueling heavy purchases of bonds in both the cash and futures markets this week.
The dollar's overnight surge was attributed to the strength of the March T-bond's momentum on early Friday following the U.S. labor data.
"The dollar is certainly encouraging us," one bond futures floor trader said at midsession after March T-bond's re-tested the day's high at the 113-00 level.
While the U.S. labor data dominated the market's attention in the morning, Rubin's comments clearly swayed the debt futures market in the afternoon.
His comments pushed the U.S. dollar lower, and forced weak longs to liquidate positions in both the bond and Eurodollar pits, traders said.
"We started tracking the dollar," one Eurodollar trader said. "Bids and offers were tied with the dollar."
A critical resistance area for June Eurodollars is pegged at 94.37 to 94.40.
While the contract tested 94.37 in reaction to the unemployment rate, average hourly earnings and the workweek, June was unable to plow through the level.

"The 94.37 to 94.40 area will be decisive," Tim Ransford, senior technical analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds, said, adding that a rally through that area would lead June to 94.71 and possibly 95.01 in the intermediate term.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were up 18/32 at 112-15/32, 10-year notes were up 13/32 at 109-16/32, June Eurodollars were up four basis points at 94.35, September Eurodollars were five bps higher at 94.22 and June T-bills were three bps higher at 94.89.
